maml:description.maml:para: Connects to a ConnectWise Control server.
Three ways to sign in:
-Credentials alone (default): Basic auth with a Control user account that does not use MFA. Gives access to every function in the module, limited by that user's permissions. Never expires.

-Credentials with -Mfa, -OneTimeCode or -TotpSecret: signs in the way the web page does, with a one-time code, for accounts that require MFA. Gives the same access as -Credentials alone. The login is a cookie that the server expires; when it does, commands fail with a permission error and you run Connect-CWC again. The password and TOTP secret are not kept after the login.

-ApiSecret: the authentication secret configured in the RESTful API Manager extension's RESTfulAuthenticationSecret setting, sent as the CTRLAuthHeader header. Works when every user account requires MFA. Only functions backed by that extension are available (see NOTES); other functions return an error telling you to connect with -Credentials.

The connection is validated before it is cached. An existing connection to the same server with the same method and identity (user and password, or secret) is reused unless -Force is given; anything else reconnects. A cached MFA login is checked with one call first and replaced with a new login if it has expired.
Control server hostname, e.g. control.example.com. A leading http(s):// is removed. HTTPS is always used.
Username and password of a Control user account.

Reconnect even when the cached connection is for the same server, method and identity. If that refresh fails, the previous connection is kept. A failed connection to a different server, method or identity leaves the module disconnected, so later commands can't reach the old server.
Control server hostname, e.g. control.example.com. A leading http(s):// is removed. HTTPS is always used.
Username and password of a Control user account.

The account's authenticator-app (TOTP) secret, for unattended scripts. The current code is computed from it at each login; the secret itself is not stored. Accepts the value Control stores for authenticator apps ("ms:" followed by Base32, as New-CWCMFA creates) or bare Base32. Not for email or SMS codes.

Keep it in a secret store, e.g. Microsoft.PowerShell.SecretManagement: -TotpSecret (Get-Secret ...). A TOTP secret stored next to the password turns MFA into a single factor: keep them in separate vaults where you can, prefer -ApiSecret when its functions are enough, and replace the secret if the computer is compromised.

maml:alert.maml:para: Functions available with -ApiSecret: Get-CWCSessionDetail, Update-CWCSessionName, Invoke-CWCCommand (queues the command; output is not retrieved), Find-CWCSession, New-CWCSession, Add-CWCSessionNote, Send-CWCSessionMessage, Send-CWCToolboxItem. Only calls that are safe to repeat (reads, "set to value" updates) are retried on HTTP 500.

The API secret is not tied to a Control user: the extension does not apply role permissions or session group scoping, so it can act on every session. Treat it like an administrator password. Requires the RESTful API Manager extension (2d558935-686a-4bd0-9991-07539f5fe749).

MFA logins are never retried automatically: each attempt counts toward the server's login limits. Errors carry an ErrorId: CWC.MfaRequired, CWC.MfaCodeRejected, CWC.LoginFailed, CWC.LoginThrottled or CWC.NoResponse. The device is never marked as trusted, and the login is never saved to disk.

maml:description.maml:para: Opens the ConnectWise Control Host client joined to a session, like Join in the web UI.

Gets a Host access token for the session (PageService.GetAccessToken), builds the client launch URL the web client uses (sc-<instance>://...) and opens it with the installed Control client. The join is recorded in the session's audit trail (InitiatedJoin), as a web UI join is.
The client must already be installed for the current Windows user: join any session once from the web UI. Launching works on Windows only; on other systems use -UrlOnly and open the URL yourself.
Requires Connect-CWC -Credentials and the JoinSession permission in -Group.
Session ID. Accepts SessionID from the pipeline (e.g. from Get-CWCSession).
Session type. Defaults to Access.
Session group containing the session. Defaults to 'All Machines' for Access, 'All Sessions' for Support and 'All Meetings' for Meeting.
Session name shown as the client's title. Taken from the pipeline (e.g. from Get-CWCSession); when given, the session lookup is skipped.

Return the launch URL instead of opening the client. The URL holds an access token: treat it like a password. It uses a delegated token that expires in 5 minutes when your role has the CreateDelegatedAccessToken permission; otherwise a regular Host token (with a warning), which is valid for the server's access token lifetime (7 days by default).

maml:alert.maml:para: The access token is not written to verbose, debug, warning or error output. It does appear in the launched client's command line (as with a web UI join), and PowerShell module or script-block logging, when enabled, can record the API response that carries it. The token is tied to the public IP address this call comes from, so the URL may not work from another network (a different proxy or VPN exit).
